text: To do whatever you do at all to the utmost perfection, ought to be your aim at this time of your life; if you can reach perfection, so much the better; but at least, by attempting it, you will get much nearer than if you never attempted it at all.
author: Philip Stanhope, 4th Earl of Chesterfield
locator: Letter XLIII, to his son, London, July 1, Old Style 1748
